gaps.sentence: Can we ___ a phone call before we leave?
gaps.explanation: make a phone call / make a call is the standard collocation.

gaps.sentence: There was ___ fog at the airport all morning.
gaps.explanation: thick fog (or dense fog) is the standard collocation; 'strong fog' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: We ___ breakfast on the terrace every morning in summer.
gaps.explanation: have breakfast/lunch/dinner is the standard collocation for eating meals.

gaps.sentence: It was three in the morning, but I was wide ___.
gaps.explanation: wide awake means completely awake; it is the fixed collocation with 'wide'.

gaps.sentence: She was bitterly ___ when her proposal was rejected.
gaps.hint: adjective collocating with 'bitterly' after bad news
gaps.explanation: bitterly disappointed is the standard collocation; 'bitterly' combines with negative feelings.

gaps.sentence: Her talk really ___ home the urgency of the situation.
gaps.explanation: 'Drive something home' = make it fully understood.

gaps.sentence: I was slightly ___ by his rude reply.
gaps.explanation: slightly annoyed is a standard collocation; the other options are too strong to be 'slight'.

gaps.sentence: If you ___ your word, people will trust you.
gaps.explanation: keep your word means to do what you promised.
